title: IdP Attribute Normalizer and Migration Guide for SAML SSO Rollouts
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Customers using different IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping) surface incompatible SAML attribute payloads which block adoption of RBAC v2 and make audit events inconsistent. Goal: deliver a single IdP Attribute Normalizer service + migration notes and runbook so teams can onboard SAML SSO with minimal customer engineering, consistent RBAC role mapping, and reliable audit logging.

Scope:
- Normalization rules for common assertion attributes (email, uid, username, groups, roles, nameID formats) across Okta/Azure/Google/Ping.
- Compatibility table and example IdP configuration snippets for each vendor.
- Migration/runbook for existing customers migrating from our legacy SSO behavior to RBAC v2 (role claim rename, group sync).
- Tests: end-to-end SAML assertion conformance suite, integration tests, and synthetic traffic to validate audit event shapes.
- Docs: Confluence onboarding doc, step-by-step Admin Console UI instructions, and an internal troubleshooting playbook.

Non-goals: SCIM provisioning backend changes (handled in ENG-51010), client-side SDK changes for SAML flows, and UI redesign of the Admin Console (separate ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Normalizer service implemented behind feature flag and enabled for Canary customers
Compatibility matrix with concrete Okta/Azure/Google/Ping examples reviewed and approved by Security
End-to-end tests added to CI that verify attribute mappings and audit event formats
Migration runbook published and linked from onboarding flow
Documentation updated in Confluence and Admin Console Help with provider-specific instructions
comments: 2026-02-11 - MC: Initial scoping meeting notes. Agreed to prioritize attribute mappings that break RBAC: groups -> roles, email vs preferred_username, and nameID formats. Action: engineering to draft normalization rules and run a 1-day compatibility sweep on 10 existing customers.

2026-02-16 - OP: PoC Normalizer implemented as a middleware in auth-service. Prototype rules: prefer 'email' claim, fallback to nameID (emailAddress or transient format), group claim keys supported: 'groups', 'roles', 'memberOf', 'appRoles'. Added simple mapping table for Okta 'groups' -> RBAC roles via regex. PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-service/pull/7345

2026-02-19 - Security (AN): Reviewed PoC. Feedback: record original raw assertion in encrypted audit blob for forensics and emit normalized audit fields (principal_email, roles_resolved, idp_vendor). Must add signature validation metrics and certificate expiry alerts. See security review comments in Confluence.

2026-02-23 - QA (JP): Added E2E tests in platform-tests to exercise Okta, Azure, Google and Ping SAML assertions using recorded samples. Found Azure sends 'http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/name' in some tenants instead of 'email'. Added test to ensure fallback to name claim. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform-tests/pull/482

2026-02-26 - OP: Compatibility notes draft: Okta: map 'email' and 'login' synonyms; recommend using Email as NameID with 'urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:1.1:nameid-format:emailAddress' for easiest mapping. Azure AD: prefer 'user.mail' if present, otherwise 'user.userprincipalname'; groups are delivered via Graph/Group memberships (needs group filtering to avoid huge payloads). Google Workspace: send 'primaryEmail' or use custom attribute 'customRoles' via SAML mapping. Ping: often uses 'memberOf' LDAP attribute; ensure group claim name is configured. Added example app config snippets per vendor to Confluence.

2026-03-01 - PM (L.Kim): Approved migration runbook checklist and escalation path. Items: (1) Notify customer about attribute name changes, (2) Provide test ACS URL and metadata, (3) Offer 1:1 onboarding session for enterprise customers with >5k users. Updated runbook link in attachments.

2026-03-02 - OP: Enabled feature-flagged normalizer for 2 canary customers (ACME Corp, BetaTech). Monitoring: onboarding-success-rate dashboard (link attached). Observed a single failure due to clock skew on Ping assertion; mitigated by increasing acceptance window to 5 minutes and documenting change in troubleshooting playbook. Next: roll to 10 customers pending audit sign-off.
